summary: Postmortem follow-up call after the 2027-09-28 inference outage. Redwood walked through root cause: autoscaler interaction with KV cache eviction caused GPU memory bloat and OOMs under a rare traffic spike. Immediate mitigations applied (hotfix to eviction logic, conservative autoscaler thresholds, manual restart runbook) and long-term work (improved observability, automated circuit-breaker, canary rollout policy updates). Meridian requested timeline for patch, a technical deep dive, and security artefacts for compliance. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-30 14:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Liam Carter, Priya Singh, Marco Delgado (Redwood); Sara Patel, Daniel Kim, Tariq Hassan, Jill Moreno (Meridian)

00:00:04 Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. We wanted to run through the postmortem follow-up and make sure the actions and timeline are clear. Sara, you ok for a quick recap from your side?
00:00:20 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Yeah, hi Liam. Thanks. Uh we've been working through the outage impacts, our support lines had a bunch of customers on the calls yesterday. The main ask is, first, confirm the root cause and when the patch will be in prod; second, we need the security docs for SOC2 evidence; and third, mitigation steps so this doesn't recur.
00:00:45 Liam (Redwood AE): Totally. Priya is going to walk through the technical root cause and the hotfix we shipped. Priya?
00:00:53 Priya (Redwood SE): Sure, thanks. Quick TL;DR: during the traffic spike on 2027-09-28 the autoscaler performed several rapid scale-outs. There was an interaction with our KV cache eviction routine — some eviction paths were skipped when pods terminated quickly, which left stale references in GPU memory. Over the course of a few minutes those references accumulated, leading to memory fragmentation and then OOMs on the inference workers. The OOMs triggered cascading restarts which looked like 502/5xx to your clients.
00:01:28 Daniel (Meridian SRE): Sorry, can you repeat the part about the eviction being skipped? We saw nodes go into Terminating and then a lot of 503s.
00:01:36 Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah so when the pod lifecycle hook ran we expected the KV cache to flush; because of a race with the autoscaler lifecycle, in some cases the eviction call didn't complete before the container was torn down. The pointer to the GPU-allocated KV buffer was left un-freed. And because our runtime keeps a shared allocator, that leaked GPU address space until the kernel reclaimed it post-crash.
00:01:58 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): So it's a memory leak caused by a race during scaling — makes sense. Did you see this on specific model families or across the board?
00:02:08 Priya (Redwood SE): Mostly on the long-context LLM variant you run for the summarization pipeline, because the longer KV entries make the allocation patterns heavier. But we also saw lower probability on other variants when request concurrency was high.
00:02:22 Marco (Redwood CSM): Just to add, the immediate mitigation we pushed was a hotfix that forces synchronous flush on preStop hook and a conservative autoscaler cool-down to prevent rapid scale churn. We rolled that yesterday evening.
00:02:36 Daniel (Meridian SRE): We noticed the error rate drop after your restart, yes. Good catch.
00:02:40 Priya (Redwood SE): Yeah the hotfix reduces the race window. For long-term we're changing the eviction code path to be idempotent and adding reference counting so an abrupt termination can't orphan buffers.
00:02:55 Tariq (Meridian Security): From the security/compliance lens, we need to understand whether any customer data was exposed, and we need the audit logs and the timeline for the mitigation steps. Also KMS key usage during the incident?
00:03:10 Liam (Redwood AE): Great question. Short answer: no evidence of data exfiltration. The incident was memory management and OOMs within the runtime; requests failed, but we don't have indications the in-flight payloads left our systems. We'll send the full audit timeline and the S3/audit exports. Marco will own that.
00:03:28 Marco (Redwood CSM): I'll pull the access logs, the request traces and the deployment history and package them with the postmortem doc. Expect that by 2027-10-04.
00:03:38 Jill (Meridian Product): Quick product question — we had customers complaining about degraded latency even before full outages. Anything planned to reduce tail latency on reloads?
00:03:49 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, two things: (1) we are introducing a circuit-breaker at the routing layer to divert traffic away from nodes with warming KV caches, and (2) we will do a warm-start for new replicas for critical routes so they warm the KV cache before receiving production traffic. These combine to reduce tail latency during scale events.
00:04:10 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): How long to implement both?
00:04:14 Priya (Redwood SE): Circuit-breaker ready in canary in about two weeks; warm-start changes in about three to four weeks. We'll run canary traffic on a small dedicated pool first.
00:04:27 Daniel (Meridian SRE): For our side, we want a rollback playbook — if we detect increasing 5xxs we want to be able to fail traffic to a dedicated fallback model or to your prior version. Is that supported today?
00:04:40 Priya (Redwood SE): We have fallback routes and version pinning. The missing piece was the automated failover to a different model family on OOM patterns — that's in our short-term plan. We can add an automatic route fallback policy that triggers on saturating OOM metrics.
00:04:53 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Also: we've been discussing Dedicated capacity with our infra folks. If we move critical production routes to dedicated GPUs would this problem be prevented?
00:05:01 Priya (Redwood SE): Dedicated helps reduce noisy neighbor and scale churn because you'd have reserved replicas; however the bug is in the eviction path which could still occur. Dedicated reduces blast radius and gives you more predictable capacity, but we still need the eviction idempotency fix.
00:05:16 Liam (Redwood AE): To be clear: Dedicated plus the patch is the strongest approach. We can scope a pilot for a single critical route if you'd like.
00:05:24 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Please do, yes. We'll get procurement and infra aligned.
00:05:30 (00:05:30) [timestamp pause]
00:05:35 Priya (Redwood SE): On observability, we added new metrics: GPU-alloc reference counts, eviction-failure counters, and an autoscaler churn metric. Those will feed into alerting so the SRE can act before memory fragmentation reaches OOM.
00:05:52 Daniel (Meridian SRE): Can you export those metrics into our Datadog? We want to create composite alerts along with our latency SLOs.
00:05:59 Marco (Redwood CSM): Yes, we can push to your Datadog account — we'll share the integration steps and sample dashboards.
00:06:06 Tariq (Meridian Security): On the compliance front: can you confirm retention of logs and whether audit exports include payload hashes only — we need to meet a regulator requirement that PII not be preserved in logs.
00:06:17 Liam (Redwood AE): We redact payloads by default in access logs and only store hashes for traceability; the full customer payloads are not retained. We'll include the log retention policy document and the exact S3 export fields.
00:06:29 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Good. Also, we had a question from legal about credits for impacted customers. What's Redwood's policy?
00:06:40 Liam (Redwood AE): We have a standard incident credit policy; for major outages we provide pro-rated credits and we can offer one-off commercial relief for customers affected beyond SLA. I'll share initial proposed credits and legal language.
00:06:54 Jill (Meridian Product): Can you also include the timing for the outage window for each customer? We need that for customer communications.
00:07:01 Marco (Redwood CSM): We'll provide a per-customer window list; Daniel, can you confirm which customers you want included?
00:07:07 Daniel (Meridian SRE): We'll send the list later today, includes the top five customers of the summarization route.
00:07:15 Priya (Redwood SE): A couple more technical notes: the root-cause patch is a code change plus a config mitigation. The code change (idempotent eviction and refcounts) is scheduled for the 2027-10-10 release train; config mitigation (forcing synchronous flush and cool-down) is already applied to your clusters.
00:07:33 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Is there a public PR or internal changelog we can reference?
00:07:38 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll share the internal changelog and a sanitized PR summary. There is no public PR; these are internal runtime changes.
00:07:47 (00:07:47) [small crosstalk] Speaker 6: yeah-huh
00:07:52 Tariq (Meridian Security): On KMS: during the incident did any key rotations or KMS calls fail? We had a related alert on our side.
00:08:00 Priya (Redwood SE): No, KMS calls were successful; the failures were at the inference worker level. We'll include KMS call logs to be certain.
00:08:08 Daniel (Meridian SRE): About regression testing — can Redwood run the scenario with our real traffic profile? We want to ensure the fix holds for our burst patterns.
00:08:17 Priya (Redwood SE): Absolutely; we'll run a 4-hour stress run with your sample profile in a staging environment and surface telemetry. We'll share the test config and outcomes.
00:08:29 Liam (Redwood AE): Timeline recap: hotfix rolled (done), config mitigations (done), postmortem doc (by 2027-10-04), canary circuit-breaker (2 weeks), eviction code release (2027-10-10 train), deep-dive (week of 2027-10-11), stress test (by 2027-10-15). Does that match what you heard?
00:08:51 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Yes that's what we need. Also can you include a runbook snippet we can paste into our incident playbook?
00:08:59 Marco (Redwood CSM): We'll include a runbook snippet with commands, alerts, and the immediate manual restart steps.
00:09:05 Jill (Meridian Product): One more feature ask: can we get more granular routing so we can pin certain tenants to low-latency pools?
00:09:13 Priya (Redwood SE): We support tenant pinning via routing policies; we can propose a dedicated pool configuration for your top tenants. That's something we can scope for the pilot.
00:09:23 Daniel (Meridian SRE): Also a note: during the incident our in-house autoscaler was also scaling; there was some friction between your autoscaler cooldowns and our orchestrator. We should sync on orchestration boundaries.
00:09:35 Liam (Redwood AE): Good point — we'll set up a small working group to align autoscaler expectations and boundary conditions. That will be part of the deep dive.
00:09:45 (00:09:45) [timestamp] Speaker 1: ok
00:09:50 Priya (Redwood SE): Technical detail — the memory fragmentation isn't just the orphaned pointer: when the allocator tries to reuse fragmented chunks we get more cache misses and degraded performance; that explains the latency degradation you saw prior to full OOMs. The refcount approach will let us free or reassign buffers more deterministically.
00:10:11 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Understood. Any risk that the refcount change introduces regressions?
00:10:17 Priya (Redwood SE): We'll run unit tests, integration tests, and the staging stress test. We'll also do a 24-hour canary run on a small production slice before wide rollout.
00:10:27 Daniel (Meridian SRE): For the canary, can we get explicit SLO gates (p50/p90/p99 latency + OOM count) to signal rollback?
00:10:36 Priya (Redwood SE): Yes, we'll propose SLO gates to trigger automatic rollback to the previous runtime if breached.
00:10:41 Tariq (Meridian Security): Back to compliance: we need the long-term mitigations in writing for our SOC2 submission — the idempotency fix, the circuit-breaker, and the additional audit exports.
00:10:53 Liam (Redwood AE): We'll include those in the postmortem and produce a separate compliance brief for your security team.
00:10:59 Marco (Redwood CSM): Action owners and dates will be in the doc.
00:11:03 Jill (Meridian Product): Quick commercial: if we expand to Dedicated for the pilot, what's the lead time?
00:11:10 Liam (Redwood AE): Typically 2–4 weeks for initial provisioning depending on GPU type; we can fast-track with a CC approval. For the pilot we can start with a smaller dedicated pool to validate stability.
00:11:21 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Ok. We'll talk to procurement.
00:11:24 (00:11:24) [quiet pause]
00:11:30 Priya (Redwood SE): Any other technical questions?
00:11:33 Daniel (Meridian SRE): Can you confirm the code change touches the allocator layer only? I'm concerned about broad runtime changes.
00:11:41 Priya (Redwood SE): The patch is limited: eviction idempotency, refcount tracking, and an additional safety check at container preStop. It's scoped to the eviction/allocator subsystem; we don't change model execution paths.
00:11:56 Sara (Meridian VP Eng): Good. That gives us confidence.
00:12:00 Liam (Redwood AE): Alright I'm going to recap and close: Marco will send postmortem and audit exports by 2027-10-04; Priya will own the runbook and the staging stress test results; we'll plan a deep dive week of 2027-10-11 and target the code release in the 2027-10-10 train with canary before wide rollout. Meridian will provide customer list and traffic profiles by 2027-10-06.
00:12:28 Priya (Redwood SE): Also note we'll add the new metrics to your Datadog export and provide dashboards.
00:12:35 Daniel (Meridian SRE): Thanks, that works.
00:12:38 Tara (Meridian Security) [misnamed in log, should be Tariq]: Appreciate the clarifications.
00:12:44 Liam (Redwood AE): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the doc and schedule invites.
00:12:50 (End of main discussion)
